title: Ad Tracking & Targeted Advertising Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to stop ad tracking and prevent targeted advertising. Learn how to protect your privacy from behavioral advertising.
intro: Advertisers use sophisticated tracking methods to build profiles about your online behavior, interests, and demographics. This checklist will help you understand how ad tracking works and take concrete steps to protect your privacy from targeted advertising.

items.task: Block third-party cookies in your browser
items.why: Third-party cookies allow advertisers to track you across multiple websites and build detailed behavioral profiles.
items.howTo: In Chrome/Edge: Settings > Privacy > Cookies > Block third-party cookies. Firefox: Settings > Privacy > Custom > Cookies > Cross-site tracking cookies. Safari: Preferences > Privacy > Prevent cross-site tracking.

items.why: While not legally binding, it signals to websites that you don't want to be tracked for advertising purposes.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy > Send 'Do Not Track' request. Firefox: Settings > Privacy > Send websites 'Do Not Track' signal. Safari: Preferences > Privacy > Website tracking > Ask websites not to track me.

items.task: Turn off personalized advertising in browser settings
items.why: Prevents your browser from sharing data with advertisers for targeted ad campaigns.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy > Ad privacy > Turn off all ad privacy features. Edge: Settings > Privacy > Choose what to clear > Turn off personalized ads. Consider using Incognito Browser for enhanced privacy.

items.task: Clear advertising IDs and stored ad data
items.why: Removes existing advertising profiles and tracking identifiers that have been stored in your browser.
items.howTo: Clear browsing data including cookies, site data, and cached files. Reset advertising ID in your browser settings or use private browsing mode consistently.

items.why: Google uses your search history, YouTube activity, and Gmail data to create detailed advertising profiles across the web.
items.howTo: Visit myaccount.google.com/adssettings. Turn off 'Ads Personalization' and delete your advertising ID. Also disable activity tracking in My Activity settings.

items.task: Opt out of Facebook advertising tracking
items.why: Facebook tracks you across websites and apps, even if you don't have an account, using pixels and social plugins.
items.howTo: Go to Facebook Settings > Ads > Ad settings. Turn off ads based on data from partners, ads based on your activity, and ads that include social information.

items.why: Amazon tracks your browsing and purchase behavior to show targeted ads across the web through their advertising network.
items.howTo: Sign in to Amazon, go to Account & Lists > Your Account > Advertising preferences. Turn off 'Personalized ads' and opt out of interest-based ads.

items.why: Microsoft collects data from Bing searches, Windows usage, and Office applications for targeted advertising.
items.howTo: Visit account.microsoft.com/privacy/ad-settings. Turn off 'Personalized ads in this browser' and 'Personalized ads wherever I use my Microsoft account'.

items.task: Reset or disable mobile advertising ID
items.why: Mobile advertising IDs allow apps to track you across different applications and share data with advertising networks.
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > Privacy & Security > Apple Advertising > Turn off Personalized Ads. Android: Settings > Privacy > Ads > Delete advertising ID or opt out of personalized ads.

items.why: Location data is used to serve geographically targeted ads and build profiles about your daily routines and interests.
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services > Location-Based Apple Ads (off). Android: Settings > Location > Location Services > Google Location Accuracy (off).

items.task: Review and disable app tracking permissions
items.why: Apps often request permission to track you across other apps and websites for advertising purposes.
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking > Allow Apps to Request to Track (off). Review individual app permissions. Android: Check app permissions in Settings > Apps and revoke advertising-related permissions.

items.why: Ad blockers prevent tracking scripts and advertisements from loading, significantly reducing your digital footprint.
items.howTo: Install uBlock Origin, AdBlock Plus, or similar extensions. Configure to block ads, trackers, and malware domains. Incognito Browser includes built-in ad blocking features.

items.task: Consider switching to a privacy-focused browser
items.why: Privacy-focused browsers have built-in protections against tracking and don't collect user data for advertising purposes.
items.howTo: Try browsers like Incognito Browser, Firefox with strict privacy settings, Brave, or DuckDuckGo Browser. These block trackers and ads by default.

items.task: Use a VPN with ad blocking features
items.why: VPNs can hide your IP address and some include DNS-level ad blocking to prevent tracking across all your devices.
items.howTo: Choose a VPN service that doesn't log activity and includes ad blocking features. Configure DNS settings to use ad-blocking DNS servers like AdGuard DNS or Cloudflare for Families.

items.task: Opt out through Network Advertising Initiative
items.why: NAI represents many major advertising networks and provides a centralized way to opt out of behavioral advertising.
items.howTo: Visit optout.networkadvertising.org and click 'Opt out of all' to disable tracking from participating advertising networks. Repeat periodically as new networks join.

items.task: Use Digital Advertising Alliance opt-out tool
items.why: DAA's tool allows you to opt out of interest-based advertising from hundreds of participating companies at once.
items.howTo: Go to optout.aboutads.info and select 'Choose all companies' then click 'Submit your choices' to opt out of participating advertising networks.

items.task: Remove your information from data broker sites
items.why: Data brokers collect and sell personal information to advertisers, contributing to detailed consumer profiles used for targeting.
items.howTo: Search for your name on sites like Whitepages, Spokeo, and BeenVerified. Follow their removal processes. Consider using a service like DeleteMe for automated removal.
